# Further reading and references {#sec-resources}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="In this unit"}
By the end of this unit, you will be able to:

- choose the appropriate documentation, specification, or portal resource for your next task;
- find the source code and the right route for package or portal support; and
- cite the `ebvcube` software, the tutorial dataset, and the underlying methods correctly.
:::

This unit brings together the resources used throughout the tutorial. Use it as a reference when you need more detail than a tutorial step provides, want to inspect the format specification, or need support with the package or portal.

## Package documentation and source code

For function-level details, use the [`ebvcube` function reference](https://rdrr.io/cran/ebvcube/man/). The [source repository](https://github.com/EBVcube/ebvcube) contains the package code, release history, and the package citation [@ebvcube2025].

The released package is available from [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/package=ebvcube). The [B-Cubed r-universe package collection](https://b-cubed-eu.r-universe.dev/packages) also lists `ebvcube` and may provide more recent builds. When reproducibility matters, record the version returned by `packageVersion("ebvcube")`.

For installation and a first working example, return to [@sec-installation]. For creating, reading, or mapping an EBVCube, the package documentation is the best next step after the relevant tutorial unit.

## Format standards and the EBV framework

The [EBVCube netCDF format specification](https://github.com/EBVcube/EBVCube-format) is the authoritative description of the file structure, required attributes, and metadata conventions. Consult it when a question concerns the contents of the netCDF file rather than how to use an R function.

The format builds on the [CF Metadata Conventions](https://cfconventions.org/Data/cf-conventions/cf-conventions-1.8/cf-conventions.html) and the [Attribute Convention for Data Discovery (ACDD)](https://wiki.esipfed.org/Attribute_Convention_for_Data_Discovery_1-3) [@cfconventions; @acdd]. For the broader scientific context, see GEO BON's [introduction to Essential Biodiversity Variables](https://geobon.org/ebvs/what-are-ebvs/) and the foundational EBV paper [@pereira2013].

## The EBV Data Portal and the tutorial dataset

Use the [EBV Data Portal](https://portal.geobon.org/) to discover published datasets, view their metadata, and begin a submission. The [dataset page for *Global trends in biodiversity (BES-SIM cSAR-iDiv)*](https://portal.geobon.org/ebv-detail?id=30) is the running example used in this tutorial. It provides the dataset metadata, available downloads, and its official citation [@martins2022].

When referring to that published dataset, cite its DOI: [10.25829/5zmy41](https://doi.org/10.25829/5zmy41). Do not cite the package in place of the dataset. The package and the EBVCube design are described in the methods paper [@quoss2022].

For the complete submission workflow, return to [@sec-uploading]. If a file is not ready to upload, repeat the checks in [@sec-validating] before creating or updating a portal submission.

## Getting help and reporting problems

For a reproducible package error or a feature request, open an issue in the [`ebvcube` GitHub issue tracker](https://github.com/EBVcube/ebvcube/issues). For a question about how to use the package, begin with the function reference and troubleshooting guide; if you need to open an issue, include the error message, `sessionInfo()`, the installed package version, and a minimal reproducible example where possible.

For a portal upload, metadata-form, review, or dataset-specific problem, use the contact route provided by the portal. The troubleshooting guide in [@sec-troubleshooting] will help you identify whether the issue belongs with the package or the portal before you ask for help.
